name: 263. OSS setup lock: scoped consent tokens and provider header references (setup-lock-e2e)
description: Opt-in profile regression for TXE-5411 (PR5 8338c04af M105 and 36f076c4c). Run with provider_config/setup-lock-temp-token/config.json (setup_token set, no enabled admin, temp-token auth and the MCP OAuth2 server on) on an isolated fresh instance, INCLUDE_PREVIEW=1, PARALLEL=0 and FEATURE=setup-lock-e2e; the harness's setup token must be the profile's (BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN, default bifrost-e2e-setup-token). Rows that must act without a credential strip the X-Bifrost-Setup-Token header the harness injects. Part 1, scoped temp tokens: while the OSS setup lock is active, an MCP consent or per-user auth temp token authorizes exactly its method, raw path and resource, as it does once dashboard auth is on, and is not the admin. Before the fix the lock answered every such request 401 'send the setup token', stranding MCP users mid-consent. Case 1 proves the lock is active; cases 2-3 register a disposable client and open a consent flow, chaining the flow id and token out of the 302 Location; case 4 reads the flow with only the token (200; red before the fix); case 5 submits mode=session with only the token and expects the consent handler's 401, not the lock's (red before the fix); cases 6-7 keep another flow and a management route at 401. Part 2, provider extra-header server-secret references: the 403 for an auth-bypassed caller that introduces or repoints an env./vault. header reference is reachable where the fail-open bypass admits a request: a gateway with no config store, enterprise builds, and (corrected by TXE-4989) an OSS gateway whose operator whitelisted the provider route, which passes the setup lock; folder 264 pins that last case over HTTP, and the handler Go tests pin the rest. Under the OSS setup lock the same caller is refused before the handler: case 8 creates a keyless custom provider with a header reference as the setup-token admin (base_url 127.0.0.1:9, nothing listens and nothing leaves the host), case 9 tries to repoint it with no credential and gets the lock's 401, case 10 shows nothing was persisted, case 11 shows an authenticated save of the unchanged reference still succeeds, and case 12 deletes the provider. The openai keyword is only a harness filter label; no provider calls are made. Cookies and redirect following are disabled. Every unexpected status fails. Run the whole folder in order.
